characters.description: A trio ofpoorly-animatedhumans: two high-school tennis players named Carlton and Troy and their coach, Mr. Kreese. They're the first humans to appear on the show in person (not counting Santa Claus, who may be a sort of elf/fairy). Ambiguously Brown: Troy has a somewhat dark skin tone, but it might just be a tan. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: In spite of their delusional behavior, Carlton and Troy are actually extremely skilled at playing tennis. The one time Gumball actually tried to return one of their serves, the spin alone was enough to tear the racket out of his hand. The Bus Came Back: After a three season long absence, Carlton and Troy finally make another prominent appearance in "The Spinoffs". A Day in the Limelight: In "The Sweaters."

characters.name: Ripley  2000 Manager
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: He was originally just aOne-Shot Characterin "The Refund", then suddenly made a reappearance in "The Question" when Larry goes mad from the realization that his life is a grind, more than two seasons later. Cartoon Creature: He has animal ears, though. Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: Either he's wearing some kind of coveralls (with teddy bear ears) orthat's part of his bodyandthe only article of clothing is his tie. Honest John's Dealership: He's sold a paper shredder claiming it was a game console. Karma Houdini: He never suffered any consequences for how he treats Larry and his customers.

characters.name: Mr. Robinson's Heart
characters.description: Allegorical Character: He's less of a character and more of a phsyical manifestation of Mr. Robinson's fear of showing his true feelings. Antagonist Title: Of Season Six's "The Heart", where he forces Mr. Robinson to not show any positive emotions. Chekhov's Gag: Remember that quick gag where Mr. Robinson's heart came out in "The Debt"? Turns out that his heart is actually it's own sentient being. Pet the Dog: He does begrudgingly admit that he felt something when Gumball and Darwin pour all their love out to him.

characters.name: Superintendent Evil
characters.description: A live-action human being who is the school's superintendent. Adoption Diss: He calls Darwin "Watter-adopted-son". Dean Bitterman: Evil is an incredible overbearing enforcer of what he considers "proper", even before showing himself to beoutright villainous. Dirty Coward: Acts like he's a threat to everyone after taking over the school. But after Gumball and Darwin free everyone from his control. He prepares to engae into a fist fight with Gumball but he then runs away like the coward he truly is. The Dreaded: Everyone is scared and intimidated by him.

characters.name: Virus
characters.description: Adaptive Ability: It's constantly mutating, causing it to gain strange properties such as flight and infecting computers instead of people. Avenging the Villain: The virus was the commander of a virus army and Sole Survivor of Gumball washing his hands. He swears he'll avenge them by infecting and killing Gumball, his family, his friends, and everyone else until "nothing is left alive on the surface of the Earth". Boisterous Weakling: Its ability to infect and control things make it genuinely dangerous, but in spite of all the boasts, it does not understand that its extremely small size makes it physically harmless to anything close to human-sized. Briar Patching: Gumball defeats him this way, using the "dares them to do it" variety. Gumball accuses the virus of being too much of a coward to try and kill him, Teri and Darwin without his army of machines, and claims he would never come out and fight him mano a mano. The virus takes the bait and leaves his machines to fight, at which point Gumball easily squishes him. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Despite being an evil virus, he did truly care for his comrades.

characters.name: The Snatcher/Vladus Lokowitchki
characters.description: Expy: He has a lot of similarities withSadako Yamamura. Go Mad from the Isolation: His sadistic curse and anger is the cause of being trapped in the mirror for so long, away from his lover and daughter. Heel–Face Turn: Breaking the mirror not only breaks Gumball's curse, but also restores Vladus back to normal. Killed Off for Real: Once he comes back to life, he tries to hug Carrie, his daughter, for the first time. Obviously, since she's a ghost, he immediately goes through her and accidentally falls out of a window. In an odd turn of events, this was actually good, as he turns into a ghost and can now physically hug her. Luke, I Am Your Father: Turns out to be Carrie Kruger's father.

characters.name: Zach
characters.description: An intolerable split personality Gumball develops upon finding out his real first name in "The Name". Asshole Victim: Gumball more or less kills Zach, albeit in self-defense and maybe by accident. Considering Zach was an independent consciousness, this might have significant moral implications... but he's such a jackass that no one gives it a second thought. Cool Cat: Zach definitelytriesto invoke the "confident" form of this trope, even wearing sunglasses, but everyone just thinks he's a tremendous douche. He even proudly declares that "There's a new cat in town!" shortly after appearing. Cool Shades: He suddenly starts wearing neon-purple rimmed shades from nowhere, whichreally aren't very cool looking, and work more likeSinister Shades. Crazy-Prepared: One genuine skill he demonstrates is planning all sorts of tricks to delay the other Wattersons, even putting a trap in his pocket for when they'd try to frisk him.

characters.name: Chanax
characters.description: Evil, Inc.: They literallystealyour soul if you work there and force you to work 24/7. During Gumball's expedition to the CEO's office, the building turns into an ominous trap-filled complex with filing cabinets try to crush you, tidal waves of paperwork to drown you, and man-eating secretaries. Laser-Guided Karma: The building finally collapses in "The Founder" and it makes no signs of recovery in later episodes. MegaCorp: Chanax's imposing presence stretches across Elmore, whether it be owning smaller businesses or to many of it's citizens working there.

characters.name: Elmore
characters.description: Not only is every individual object in the Elmore alive and sentient, but Elmore in its totality seems to possess some sort of intelligence. Although it hasn't talked or shown a face like any of the others objects or the planets, "The Void" heavily implies the world itself was responsible for the void's creation and "mistakes" being sent into it. Acid-Trip Dimension: Can certainly come off like this, asvariously colored,variously animatedtalking animals,talking food,talking anthropomorphic objects and phenomena,talking objects that are literally just objects, andwhatever else the animators could come up with, all coexist and interact in a world of live-action backgrounds, creating possibly one of the most bizarre worlds ever constructed for any cartoon. Allegorical Character: Its modus operandi is pretty much that of an author who doesn't mindchanging their world retroactivelyor doing terrible things to their characters for the sake of making the story more interesting. The Bad Guy Wins: Maybe not "bad", but it can be considered an antagonist. And regardless, it succeeded in drawing Elmore into The Void in the season 6 finale.Or it would have if the show hadn't been revived, ensuring Elmore's safety, for now... Cloudcuckooland: A suburb of unrelenting weirdness, whereRule of FunnyandMedium Blendinggovern and logic and common sense are irrelevant. Not just that, but it is also sentient and can banish residents toThe Voidjust for being boring.

characters.name: Elmore Junior High
characters.description: Academy of Adventure: The school is teeming with all sorts of strange students and insane adults that Gumball and Darwin frequently interact with.A lotof episodes in the show take place here. Sucky School: Elmore Jr. High is not a school you'd want to be in. The people running it are all either insane, neurotic, or too apathetic to care, or even all three of these combined. Many students have all sorts of strange abilities and powers. The school isregularlydestroyed by its students, teachers, or natural elements. At one point, the school had to merge with aprisonto keep it running.

characters.name: Kip Schlezinger
characters.description: The main news anchor of Elmore News. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He does not appear on TV again after "The News" and is entirely phased out from the show by Season 7. A Day in the Limelight: "The News". Jerkass: A more lighter example than most, but many scenes show that he can be quite rude and insensitive. Such as when he pranked Phil on live TV. Kent Brockman News: He's the star of Elmore News.

characters.name: Mike the Microphone Guy and Ken
characters.description: The on-set news reporter whose head is the microphone and isn’t attached to his body. He holds his head up to people to interview them. He is friends with his cameraman, Ken. A humanoid with a camera for a head A Day in the Limelight: "The News". The Determinator: Mike would let himself get eaten by Evil Turtle's babies if it meant the got good coverage of the outbreak. Lack of Empathy: Mike and Ken remained entirely unfazed over Gary getting eaten by Evil Turtle. Meaningful Name: Mike is amicrophone.

characters.name: Phil
characters.description: Elmore New's weatherman. Also works at Chanax. Butt-Monkey: Gets pranked by Kip on live-TV. It's implied that he does this regularly to him. Cartoon Creature: Likely just another colorful blob person like the Parhams and Marvin. The Eeyore: Working in aSoul-Crushing Desk Jobat Chanax and being pranked on TV has left him a tad depressed and rather unemotional in "The Founder". He perks up in the end. Hidden Depths: In "The Founder", he discovers that he really loves dancing.

characters.name: Barry
characters.description: A human (most versions)/foam finger puppet (US version only) that hosts the sports sections. He loves his job a little too much. Animate Inanimate Object: One of those giant foam fingers you put on your hand during a sports event. Department of Redundancy Department: His schedule:9:30am: sports1:30pm: more sports4:30pm: SPOOOORTS NO INDOOR VOICE:SPOOOOOOOOOOORTS!!!! One-Word Vocabulary: Only ever says "SPOOOOOOOOOORTS!!!"

characters.name: Alison Sandra Gator
characters.description: A lonely elderly crocodile lady with a pet cat named Martin who she believes is a "real boy". She is usually kind of mean. She is pretty desperate for love because she's been saving herself for marriage her whole life. She always feeds pigeons because she's an old lady. Crazy Cat Lady: She has a cat named Martin and in "The Butterfly", she says she has more cats. A Dog Named "Cat": Despite her name, she's actually a crocodile. Freudian Excuse: She acts like a jerk sometimes but it may be because she's so lonely and lives in squalor. Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: A crocodile who wears clothes.

characters.name: Blue-Haired Lady
characters.description: Limited Wardrobe: Slightly averted, she has a casual outfit she wears when not working and a business suit she wears when on the job. New Job as the Plot Demands: Works at the movie theater ("The Anybody", "The Ghouls"), a flight attendant in Darwin’s hypotheticalImagine Spotin "The Sucker", at the Rainbow Factory ("The Web"), Chanax Inc, ("The Founder") Remember the New Guy?: Kinda just showed up in the beginning of the sixth season of the series but immediately became as frequent as characters like Ms. Combs, Karen, the construction men, Pantsbully, etc. who’ve been around since Season 1 or 2.

characters.name: Bandage doctor
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: He’s a living adhesive bandage. Dr. Jerk: Sometimes can be this, but often falls underReasonable Authority Figure. No Name Given: His actual name is never stated.

characters.name: Clown
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: Played with. He's the spotlight character during the climax of "The Curse of Elmore", but is actually Tobias in disguise. Hidden in Plain Sight: In "The Curse of Elmore", it's revealed that he watcheseveryonein town and has been doing it for a long time. Hidden in the background where no one will notice. Monster Clown: An odd non-antagonistic version. He's scary, has a deep voice, and creepily stalks people - yet, he has never actively (or intentionally) ever hurt someone.

characters.name: Construction Men
characters.description: Three LEGO-like men who are construction workers, and sometimes take other jobs. The red one is called Hank, the gray one's name in unknown, and the blue one is called Steve. Hank has a son named Bobby, and an unnamed wife. There is an unnamed yellow one, who appears in "The Shell", "The Choices", "The List", "The Blame," and "The Factory" and is one of the Sphere Citizens (see Extremely Minor Characters page). Animate Inanimate Object: LEGO-like plastic toys. Construction Catcalls: Played with. They're genuinely trying to compliment everyone they see during their job, but it comes off as beingperverseandmean. Gumball tries to straighten them out in "The Misunderstandings". Does Not Know His Own Strength: Hank and the gray man in "The Butterfly". Fully-Dressed Cartoon Animal: They wear overalls and shoes.

characters.name: Elmore Police
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: All of them are fast food. Earl is a hot dog (with an almost identical design to Hot Dog Guy and "Porky" Cassidy), Hamburger Cop is ahamburger, there's a lot of French fry officers, there's a few coffee cups, and there's a soda can. Funny Animal: One rarely seen officer is a dog who never speaks, only pants and barks. Gender Flip: The coffee cop was originally a male but was changed to a female in "The Heist". Although it's been shown that there's more than one coffee cop. Police Are Useless: They're rarely competent. The only sign of competence one of them has shown was the coffee cup in " The Shippening" when she suggested that they go back and pick up the piece of evidence (the magic notebook) that was dropped from the Awesome Store van, but Donut Cop misheard her and thought she said to get ice cream and chicken. The Smurfette Principle: The coffee cop is the only female member of the police force as.is Season 5.

characters.name: Hairy Hobo
characters.description: A hairy hobo wearing a trench coat. He wears a hat that he also uses to collect donations. He is kind of eccentric. Ambiguously Gay: In "The Misunderstandings", he thinks Gumball asked him out on a date and he happily accepts. However Gumball's twelve years old and he's at least a middle aged man, so this rather concerning. Cartoon Creature: He may be the same species as Principal Brown. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Like in "The Faith", "The Gripes", "The Misunderstandings", "The Saint", and the times where he chose to spend the little money he has on going to the movies (three times) or taking the public bus. Continuity Nod: In "The Castle", he stole Gumball's clothes. In "The Plan", his next appearance (in Gumball's imagination), Gumball imagines him wearing his clothes.

characters.name: Ms. Combs
characters.description: A lady who did a lot of internet dating, but is now in a relationship with the cowboy. She also works at the mall and Chanax. When she works at the mall she wears a shirt. She also has a different default pose when she's standing than other characters, seen in her picture. She became the school guidance counselor in "The Labels", giving everyone labels which cause them to become caricatures of their worst traits, and tries to take over the school. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: She has a gold chain belt and a gold chain necklace. Cartoon Creature: She's a skinny black humanoid with a hexagon for a head and waist and skinny limbs. Distracted by the Sexy: Marvin is because of her in "The Tag". Previously, in "The Watch", they went on a date but he was too old for her. In "The Shippening", Sarah ships them together. Jerkass Ball: In "The Schooling" she goes insane and beats people like Tony up to get a better deal on something. In "The Intelligence" she tries to force Gumball and Darwin to tell her where the Internet is.

characters.name: Jeff and Susan Benson
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: Living corn cob and mushroom. New Job as the Plot Demands: Jeff works at Chanax ("The Founder"), the Rainbow Factory (in both the paperwork and physical labor sides, "The Kids", "The Worst", "The Deal", "The Web", "The Factory") , as an auctioneer ("The Misunderstandings", "The Boredom"), and as a mailman ("The Slip"). Nice Guy: Jeff is is some episodes. No Social Skills: Jeff seems to have developed this trait in Season 6, making him corny to fit his appearance. Plant Person: They mention needing good soil to plant their kids in "The Sale".

characters.name: Karen
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: She is called "honey" on at least one occasion by Larry. Anthropomorphic Food: She is a pink pear with pigtails. Cephalothorax: She has one, considering the fact her head and neck are also her body. Justified, as she is a fruit. Girlish Pigtails: She has these, but also had a ponytail with bangs when she was younger. Jerkass Ball: She attacks Gumball in "The Oracle" and went insane and beats people up in "The Schooling". In "The Intelligence" she tries to force Gumball and Darwin to tell her where the Internet is.

characters.name: Leonard Daniels
characters.description: A small yellow lightbulb who says "I don't mind" after being injured or when he does something for somebody. He also works at the Rainbow Factory and as a mailman. Ambiguously Related: Bernice, his gender opposite look alike. It's not clear if she's his sister, wife, or just a friend who happens to be of the same species. Animate Inanimate Object: A weird yellow lightbulb. Ascended Extra: Downplayed. He was originally aOne-Shot Characterin "The Awkwardness", but became aRecurring Extrain the following seasons. Catchphrase: "I don't mind."

characters.name: Martha Miller
characters.description: Alliterative Name:MarthaMiller. Anthropomorphic Food: A talking pink cupcake with sprinkles. Everyone Has Standards: While she usually keeps herselfcomposed, she screams in terror after seeing the effects of the makeup onGumball. Recurring Character: Usually appears to fill up the background. Ship Tease: "The Love" hints that she has feelings for Gary.

characters.name: Martin Peaches
characters.description: A chocolate cupcake with sprinkles. A rather annoying citizen who is bad at whatever job he is assigned for the episode. Anthropomorphic Food: A talking cupcake. Jerkass: Comes across as one of the more ruder people in town. Not taking any of his jobs seriously and annoying clients and customers when he is bored. In "The Heist" he tries to pass himself as a hero to the police after a bank robbery and tries topin the blame on Larry. Pale Females, Dark Males: Martha Miller, the female cupcake, has pale pink frosting, and Martin Peaches, the male cupcake, has dark brown frosting. Pet the Dog: In "The Founder" he comforts Tony after accidentally scaring him with his dinosaur phobia.

characters.name: Mayor of Elmore
characters.description: The mayor of Elmore, who looks like a human but with a horribly oversized head. Ambiguously Human: He looks like a human, but is 2D animated and hasextremelyexaggerated proportions. Corrupt Politician: In private, he's flat-out admitted to putting people with money ahead of his electorate. Gonk: His enormous head has a creepy level of detail to it. Icy Blue Eyes: His eyes are light blue, and contribute to a cold stare that betrays hisconstant smiling.

characters.name: Melted Cheese Guy
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: He’s made of cheese. Big Eater: Frequently seen in fast food places like Joyful Burger. Fat Bastard: As described below, he seems to have a tendancy to take advantage of service workers to fulfill his desires with him not having to do a thing. Fat Slob: He wears only underpants, his buttcrack is always hanging out and apparently very smelly according to Bobert in "The Loophole", in "The Schooling" he demands Darwin (while filling in as the mailman for Larry) climb into his window, unbox his nail clippers, andclip his nailsfor him while claiming thatthe website said he doesnt have to lift a finger. He also uses a chair while waiting in line at Joyful Burger in "The Slip". Lazy Bum: As described above.

characters.name: Mr. Russo
characters.description: Bit Character: He only made two short appearances thus far and mainly exists to show what Jamie and Coach's family life is like. Cartoon Creature: He's a short green troll-like being with little horns, probably where Jamie's bull like traits come from. House Husband: Implied to be, since he isn't shown at a public job and comes to greet Jamie and Coach when they come home from school. Nice Guy: He seems very positive and friendly, unlike his wife and daughter. He also immediately rushes to help a man choking in the street. Parental Obliviousness: His only real negative quality so far seems to be that he takes no notice that his daughter's a bullying terror or that his wife's an egotistical unfair instructor.

characters.name: Mr. Yoshida
characters.description: Bad Boss: He gives everyone but Nicole (including an inanimate plant) an Employee of the Month award, because having a picture of a woman in the office would apparently distract all the men. Although he changes his mind in “The Deal,” so he must’ve had achange of heart. Out of Focus: He doesn't appear at all in episodes about his company ("The Factory") or his family ("The Gourmet").

characters.name: Pantsbully
characters.description: Cartoon Creature: A bean-like blob. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Look at his current design and compare withhis Season 1 design◊. It changed very drastically. Half-Dressed Cartoon Animal: Underwear, a hat, and boots. Hidden Depths: According to "The Debt", he knows CPR, suggesting he is, or was, a medical doctor. Informed Attribute: He is portrayed as fat in "The Dress", "The Sidekick” and "The Limit", but, he doesn't look overweight for a bean (which is what he's meant to look like). Especially considering he has extremely skinny limbs.

characters.name: Paperball/Mr. Chanax
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: A talking ball of crumpled paper. Mean Boss: A flashback in "The Future" shows how much he overworked poor Banana Barbara. Constantly giving her menial tasks every second,some of them being outright impossible, with no break. He worked her so hard that her brain literally explodes and entered a neverending "burnout" mode. Minor Major Character: For being such an irrelevant character, he directly causes two major events.He's responsible for effectively destroying Banana Barbara's mind and giving her the ability to predict the future.The death of his alter-ego causes Goblin to become anAscended Extraas the new CEO. He's responsible for effectively destroying Banana Barbara's mind and giving her the ability to predict the future. The death of his alter-ego causes Goblin to become anAscended Extraas the new CEO.

characters.name: "Porky" Cassidy
characters.description: Identical Stranger: To Hot Dog Guy, and to a slightly lesser extent, Earl, the hot dog cop. Uncatty Resemblance: His dog is a hot dog like him.

characters.name: Prison Quartet
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: One is a butter knife and one is a spray-paint can. Funny Animal: One of them is a dolphin. Our Goblins Are Different: One is a goblin. Interestingly, the CEO Goblin has almost the exact same character design with a different outfit, so either they're the same character or areidentical strangers. Recurring Extra: They are mostly background characters.

characters.name: Quattro and Siciliana Pepperoni
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: Pizzas. Beware the Nice Ones: In "The Understanding",they are revealed to be anarchists, as mentioned above. Book Dumb: "The Understanding" reveals they are pretty stupid at homeschooling their unintelligible son Peter, they believe the Earth is flat,their dislike of the government's laws is absolutely bonkers and honestly believed taking down a bunch of paper files would completely destroy laws forever, and they have never heard of theInternetbefore. A Day in the Limelight: In "The Understanding," where they reveal their government-hating ideals and rob Elmore City Hall. Every Pizza Is Pepperoni: They are pepperoni pizzas.

characters.name: Shape People
characters.description: Speaking Simlish: They speak similarly to that ofQ*bert. Would Hurt a Child: Ed (the blue triangle) was willing to beat up Gumball, a twelve year old. Granted Gumball misused his simlish language and incorrectly made several hurtful comments about him and his family.

characters.name: Tony
characters.description: Big Eater: Frequently seen eating fast food. Fat Slob: Less than the Melted Cheese Guy, as he seems to be less of an indulgent lazy hedonist (always jogging, not being a lazy asshole), and more aware of his horrible way of life, but he still has a lot of slobbish traits. Limited Wardrobe: Slightly averted. He has two outfits, a wife beater withno pants or shoes, and a pink tracksuit with top, bottom and shoes. Sudden Name Change: He was called Martin Peaches (although on a background news report that was barely audible) in "The Nest", and was called Tony by the cupcake guy (who was, weirdly, also named Martin Peaches in aFreeze-Frame Bonusin "The Worst") in "The Founder". They Killed Kenny Again: Blown up and disintegrated by Gumball'sSuper-Speedin "The Traitor".

characters.name: Twitchy Scientist
characters.description: It Amused Me: He injected Gumball and Darwin a serum that causes severly disturbing cases ofBody Horrorfor no real reason other than to just see what would happen to them. Karma Houdini: He's last seen about to flee Elmore, getting off scot free for his amoral experiments aside from getting fired from his experiment with Gumball and Darwin, Mad Doctor/Mad Scientist: Like you would not believe. He admitted to subjecting his patients toinvoluntaryhead transplants. Pig Man: A lanky humanoid pig who happens to be a scientist/doctor. The World Is Not Ready: He believes that Elmore isn't ready for his ways.

characters.name: Cartax
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: "The Routine", where he acts as Richard's noble steed. It Can Think: Up until "The Routine", were led to believe that Cartax was just an inanimate object. It's actually alive and acts like a horse. In his thoughts however, he speaks in a very eloquent manner. Shout-Out: His name is a pretty explicit shoutout toArtax. Undying Loyalty: To Richard. Even if he is aware that everyone sees him as a lazy idot, he will always be his master.

characters.name: Daisy the Donkey
characters.description: Alliterative Name:Daisy theDonkey. Creepy Doll: Anais' doll is this to an extreme. It's originallyPlayed for Laughsin "The World" where her doll creepily reveals that she's alive, causing Anais to scream in horror and kicks her away (which came right after a wholesome montage where the two bonded). It's thenPlayed for Horrorin "The Night". The Daisy doll has fantasies of torturing Anais,who is stuck as a doll. Expy: Daisy is combination ofMickey MouseandBarney the Dinosaur. Nice Character, Mean Actor: The Daisy on the Daisy the Donkey Show. She once had a meltdown on live TV claiming that she's superior to everyone else on the show and that they're holding her back before getting into a fight.All because one of the actors wanted to improvise their script.

characters.name: Dodj or Daar
characters.description: Dodj or Daar(Dodge or Dare) is a homemade board game Gumball and Darwin made when they were younger. The basic gist of the game is to reach the end of the board. In order to move, the player must take a "daar" card and complete a challenge. Failing to do so, or refusing to do it punishes the player with a "dodj" card. Despite its simple structure, it is actually a very powerful and dangerous game. "The Game" heavily implies that the titular game is actually sentient. And I Must Scream: As Anais discovers, one of the potential "dodj" cards has the player freezing in place until the game is over. If no one completes the game, it can be assumed that the player will be stuck like that forever. Artifact of Doom: A reality warping game that can harshly destroy a player's life. Body Horror: Poor Nicole gets two of those cards. The "You will doubt every thought you have" card sprouts a grotesque head on her forehead and the "Giant Hands" card turned her hands freakishly large. Cerebus Retcon: Was originally aRunning Gagthroughout the first season. In season two however, we learnwhy Gumball and Darwin have stopped playing this game.

characters.name: The Planets
characters.description: In the universe of this show, it's not just things on Earth that are alive, but Earth itself and other celestial bodies. The Friend Nobody Likes: Pluto. The planets make fun of her and don't care about her feelings due to no longer being classified as a planet.She finds new friends with a bunch of asteroids. Genius Loci: They're capable of thinking, speaking both with each other and people on Earth, and singing. Smug Super: They're bigger than you, will live longer than you, and flat out tell Gumball that his life and everyone else's are insignificant. What they don't get is that even their existence is finite, and end up wasting the rest of their lives rubbing their superiority into the face of someone who can't hear them. The Smurfette Principle: Out of the planets, Pluto is the only female one (notable by her voice and eyelashes).

characters.name: Gumball's Brain
characters.description: Yes, even Gumball's brain can be considered its own character. Despite being all brains, he'sGumball'sbrain, so he's not that smart. Allegorical Character: Is made one after his debut episode. Despite being a sentient character outside of Gumball, he never really becomes physically relevant anymore and mostly serves as Gumball inner conscience. Butt-Monkey: Like Gumball, he was constantly belittled by everyone over his low intelligence. He gets better. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Initially a recurring gag character but has since physically disappeared in seasons five and six. He is mentioned in several episodes though. A Day in the Limelight: His debut appearance, The Genius.

characters.name: Anime Bride Gumball and Groom Darwin
characters.description: Anime-styled humanized versions of (female) Gumball and Darwin, who are getting married. Despite being pretty minor characters, they make one hell of an impact to the audience. They are created by Sarah using the magical notebook. Butt-Monkey: Anime Darwin gets brutally crumpled up like paper, torn to shreds, lit on fire, and then doused by water, leaving him a mushy mess.He says that he's still alive and in a lot of pain. Cat Girl: Gumball is genderswapped here. The Cover Changes the Gender: Sarah reimagined Gumball as female so that he and Darwin could have a heteronormative marriage. However, she still came up with un-genderbent ships ofNicole and Yuki, as well as Larry and Mr. Small.noteMr. Small has flirted with Larry outside of this episode,but it didn't go well. Gender Flip: Anime Bride Gumball appears to be female.

characters.name: Bernie and Ethel Klein
characters.description: Two elderly goat siblings from Glory, Minnesota who have "toured" around Elmore. The Wattersons mistake them for a couple. Funny Animal: Fainting goats. Nice Guy: They're both nice and polite. They don't even seem that mad that the Wattersons tried to scam them (though they still refused to pay them). Of Corpse He's Alive: Nicole and Richard thought they killed them (when really, they're fainting goats, so they were just catatonic for a few hours). In order to save themselves from being caught, they make a convoluted plan to pose their bodies in several vacation photos and throw them into a subway, covering their tracks and becoming someone else's problem. Of course, they wake up right when their final phase was almost finished. One-Shot Character: They only appear in "The Ad".

characters.name: The Bobert Store
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: The spokesman in their Bobert upgrade commercial is a live-action man. However, when Gumball, Darwin, and Bobert visit the store, the employees, Cody and Jaden, are white figures who blend into the blinding blank environment. It's not clear if this is a weird company uniform or if they're actual living silhouettes. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Cody lets slip that theydeliberatelydesign their products to fail so consumers are forced to buy upgraded models, before he's dragged into the back and replaced by Jaden. The Faceless: Cody and Jaden are so blended into the white store interior that they're invisible. Incompetence, Inc.: Besides the above underhanded tactics, their "upgrades" are prone to glitching, faulty commands, and sudden freezing. They're also terrible at securing their cargo by plane, as all it takes is Darwin giving a small knock for the entire hatch to unload. Minor Major Character: They only appear in "The Upgrade", but they contribute to the show significantly, having created Bobert, one of Gumball's main friends.

characters.name: Brydie
characters.description: Did Not Get the Girl: She understandably turns down Rocky. Recurring Extra: After her one appearance in season 5, she made a couple background appearances in the sixth season. What the Hell, Hero?: She viciously calls out Rocky (also Gumball and Darwin) for the various illegal actions he took in the name of "their" love.

characters.name: The Chimera
characters.description: Bizarre Taste in Food: He eats hair. Detachment Combat: Although he doesn't use them to fight, The Friend can remotely control his detachable pieces and reassemble himself at will. He shows this off by taking his head off then comes together again after being blown to pieces. Does Not Know His Own Strength: He barely nudges a pinata and it's sent flying into the sky. Living Toy: An old toymaker made him because he was lonely. Misunderstood Loner with a Heart of Gold: After his creator died, he started wandering around at random and his appearance made people scared of him even though he's actually quite nice.

characters.name: Chris Morris
characters.description: One-Shot Character: Only appears in "The Burden". Pet the Dog: He hides Gumball and Darwin from the school faculty and police, sparing them from being charged with animal cruelty and being sent to prison. Smarter Than You Look: He's nearing his death, constantly out of breath, and can barely move more than an inch per minute. Yet, he's still smart enough to trigger a gas explosion in the science lab using an exposed lamp wire and a plug. Not to mention that he somehow survived a day-and-a-half alone without food and water when left at school during the weekend. Walking the Earth: Once he is finally freed by Gumball, he peacefully walks away into the wilderness, fully ready to pass on when he needs to.

characters.name: Mr. Cuddles
characters.description: Penny's pet tarantula. In "The Date", Patrick accidentally flushed him down the toilet, leading everyone to think he's dead. During his funeral, Gumball manages to get him back. Fluffy the Terrible: Despite the name, he's a tarantula, and a fairly aggressive one. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: What's Gumball's reward for rescuing him?Getting bit by him multiple times and getting hospitalized of course! Non-Standard Character Design: Somehow manages to be this despite this show having no real central art style. He's a realistic looking and anatomically correct spider. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "The Date". Though he's a part of theCrowd Songin "The World".

characters.name: Fake Muriel
characters.description: A black-and-white 1920s-styled humanoid. Gumball uses her face as his profile to catfish Louie, in a really perplexing way to give him more friends online without actually being friends. Hartman Hips: Has a quite exaggerated lower body.noteEmphasis on exaggerated Minor Major Character: Gumball uses her as his fake online profile picture. Leading Louie to immediately befriend him online and making Granny Jojo think that he's having an affair with someone. She doesn't even say asingle line. No Name Given: The closest we have to her name is Gumball's fake name he made for her. One-Shot Character: Her biggest role is in "The Catfish" and only makes two cameos later on.

characters.name: GWORP
characters.description: When Tobias briefly took over the show, he introduced GWORP, a new major character within the show. Kid-Appeal Character: As Sarah puts it, he's "the lovable alien" that draws in the viewers. Living Toy: A grey talking toy robot that came out of a Christmas present. One-Shot Character: Is a gag character that only appears in one scene in "The Test". Riddle for the Ages: What is GWORP, exactly? Where did Tobias find him? What happened to him after Gumball took back the "sitcom of life"? None is explained and unlikely to ever be.

characters.name: Hank
characters.description: A pixelated creature who happens to be Fuzzy'sYanderebest friend. Large and in Charge: He's much taller than Fuzzy and is clearly the dominant one of their (mostly one-sided) friendship. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "TheBFFs". Villainous Rescue: An unintentional example. He decides to capture and bring Fuzzy back to his place. Not to save Gumball and Darwin, but to keep him for himself.

characters.name: The Hillbilly Family
characters.description: Captain Ersatz: They're practically a copy of the family fromThe Hills Have Eyes (1977)minus being actual cannibals. Good All Along: They're not crazy cannibals. They're a genuinely nice family. Hillbilly Horrors: They may be good, but my god are they unsettling to be around. EvenAnais and Nicoleget too creeped out by them and believe that they're going to murder and eat them. Misunderstood Loner with a Heart of Gold: The family lives in isolation in the desert. The Wattersons believe that they're actually crazy cannibals who are planning chop them up in their sleep. The hillbillies are actually extremely nice and cordial with them and wish no harm on them. One-Shot Character: Only appear in "The Vacation".

characters.name: Jodie Mallard
characters.description: Anorange duckwho appears in "The Parasite". Anais forces her to be her friend, and they eventually fuse into a parasitic entity. In the end, she just wanted a pen from Anais. She makes a cameo in "The Pact". Her surname is revealed in "The Agent". Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: An orange duck. Bait-and-Switch: She's not the parasite, Anais was the real social parasite. Big Ol' Unibrow: She has two eyebrows, but they are stuck together. Black Bead Eyes: She has them.

characters.name: Josh
characters.description: Agreen humanoidwho is Anais' friend, and just like her, is socially awkward. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Played with. Josh is mostly a nice albeit socially awkward person who genuinely wants to be Anais's friend.Unfortunately he happens to be part of whats likely a doomsday cult and wants to indoctrinate Anais, with it being likely that's why he became friends with her in the first place. A Day in the Limelight: In his debut episode "The Guy". He strikes anOdd Friendshipwith Anais. Easily Forgiven: He instantly forgives Anais for all her paranoid behavior over him after seeing just how distraught she is and how desperate Gumball and Darwin have become to get him back. Foreshadowing: His strange pyramid hat and shirt are the telltale symbolsthat he's in a cult.

characters.name: Little Teddy
characters.description: A fictional talking bear and the main character of a disturbing PSA video called "Watch Out, Little Teddy". Born Unlucky: Anything bad that can possibly happen to him,happens to him. A Dog Named "Dog": A little teddy named Little Teddy. Ridiculously Cute Critter: Hilariously subverted. His design is supposed to invoke this, but thederangedandLimited Animationof the video makes him look very uncanny and weird. It's enough to leave Mr. Small ablubbering, screaming mess,after watching the video. Small Role, Big Impact: His misfortune becomes the catalyst for Darwin's eventual takeover of Elmore in his campaign to make the world safe.

characters.name: Mario
characters.description: Flat Character: The whole point of his character is to be analmostexact copy of Super Mario, but not the one that everyone thought he was. One-Shot Character: Only appeared in "The Uncle". Shout-Out: Aside from the obvious, the basis of his character is likely a sly reference to the "My uncle works at Nintendo" jokes seen online. Small Role, Big Impact: He appears for less than a minute yet the entire episode is about Gumball trying to suck up to Ocho to meet (what he thought) wastheMario.

characters.name: Parole Officer
characters.description: A literal rule parol officer who shows up for the Wattersons' family portrait. At the moment, she was also dating Frankie Watterson. Affably Evil: She's very nice and soft-spoken, but it doesn't take away from the fact she was dating Frankie, a convict (whom she was also supposed to be supervising) nor that her first instinct when Frankie runs away is to blame the family and get them swatted. Bespectacled Cutie:Played With. She is cheerful, courteous and has a pair of glasses, but being nice doesn't mean she's agoodperson, as her actions can attest. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing:Downplayed. Her shady credentials are out in the open from the moment she appears (datingFrankieis a red flag), but she's genuinely nice to the family, that is until her job is threatened which leads her to report the family as accomplices to cover herself. Dark Mistress: An unusually friendly example to Frankie. They're datingwhileshe's still his parole officer.

characters.name: Peter Pepperoni
characters.description: A pepperoni boy who is a new student in Elmore Junior High. Nobody understands what he says. Alliterative Name:PeterPepperoni. Anthropomorphic Food: He's made of pepperoni. Early-Bird Cameo: He first appears briefly in a screen in "The Spinoffs", from a scene from "The Understanding" which came after. 11th-Hour Ranger: He only joined in the middle of the sixth season.

characters.name: Rainbow Factory Shareholders
characters.description: The two animate piggybank shareholders of Rainbow Factory, Nicole's workplace. In "The Factory", they debate whether or not they should close the factory. Animate Inanimate Object: They look like pigs at first. But on closer inspection, they're piggybanks. Anti-Villain: They may be vile, greedy, and incredibly amoral, but they're not necessarily "bad guys" like the other antagonists in the show. In the end, they decide not close the factory and go through with their promise of treating their emotionally drained workers better. Gluttonous Pig: Though we never see them eat, they're appearance is quite portly. I Have No Son!: One of them disowned his son after he went "over budget" on the amount of hugs he can receive.

characters.name: Richwood High Duo
characters.description: Ascended Extra: The two were random background characters in "The Sweaters". But in "The Extras", they're the spotlight recurring segment. Butt-Monkey: They spend the entire match dealing with their literal limited movement and have to flee the stadium when one of them gets smart enough to become more animated, to the disgust of theFaceless Masses. Limited Animation: Deconstructed andPlayed for Laughs. They were intended to be faceless background characters in the show. So when the audience gets to see them move, they're juststatic images that move around. It's hard to live their lives when they can't move their limbs, fingers, eyes, or mouths. No Name Given: Probably to add on to their intentional unimportance. True Companions: They truly care about each other. When one gets run out of town when he became smart enough to become more animated, the other one still loyally follows.

characters.name: Santa Claus
characters.description: Brutal Honesty: In his amnesiac state, he ruthlessly tells Darwin and Anais why their wishes won't come true. The Bus Came Back: He makes a brief reappearance in "The Future". Easily Forgiven: Subverted. He may have been kind to the Wattersons in the end of "Christmas," but "The Finale" shows that he is actually still quite mad at them for accidentally running him over. Large Ham: When he gets over his amnesia, he goes into full-on, unmistakableBRIAN BLESSEDmode. Phosphor-Essence: He has a bright, shiny glow to him that is especially noticeable in the night scenes.

characters.name: Shadow Person
characters.description: Hate Sink: He's a nasty piece of work who mugs Gumball then rubs it in his face with an evil grin before getting away, causing him to experience aHeroic BSoD. Thankfully, he gets his comeuppance at the end when Nicole catches him trying to break into her car. Karma Houdini Warranty: He gets away with mugging Gumball and continues his crime spree via carjacking... But finds out the hard way that the car belongs toNicole. Knight of Cerebus: The time he has onscreen in "The Comic" wassurprisingly darkfor what was supposed to be a lighthearted episode of Gumball and Darwin becoming the superheroes from Sarah's comic, causing the episode to become dramatic what with Gumball giving up on his superhero career. Laser-Guided Karma: He robs Gumball and attempts to break into their car only to suffer aNo-Holds-Barred Beatdownby Nicole. Living Shadow: He’s a sentient shadow creature who has no light reflecting on his body.

characters.name: The Stink Ape
characters.description: Expy: Is effectively this show'sBigfoot. Uncertain Doom: We last see it falling in one of Mr. Small's traps. One that he says is more brutal than the others.

characters.name: Wolf and Ostrich
characters.description: Captain Ersatz: They look almost like carbon copies of Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner. Mean Character, Nice Actor: Wolf is the main antagonist of the cartoon, but he's actually quite nice when talked too normally. He was shockingly patient with Darwin's overbearing censorship. One-Shot Character: They only appear for one scene in "The Safety". Though they make a brief cameo in "The Heist".

characters.name: Wunderklopp
characters.description: Bait-and-Switch: When the Wattersons run out of food and money, they hungrily stare at Wunderklopp, who is grazing in the backyard. Cut to the Wattersons eating grass with him. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "The Ad". Running Gag: He randomly appears in many scenes, as if he's part of the family's antics.

characters.name: Characters / The Amazing World Of Gumball The Wattersons Gumball And Darwin
characters.description: Abstaining from Rudeness: He attempts this in both "The Test" and "The Roast", holding back his natural instincts to criticize and mock others. Both times, this quickly proves itself to be detrimental to his physical health, requiring him to ultimately vent all the pent-up venom he's been holding in. Absurd Phobia: Gumball loathes being filthy to any amount, which makes a certain amount of sense because he's a cat. One drop of anything on him that isn't clean water tends to get him upset, annoyed or saddened in seconds. This fear gets over-exemplified in "The Cage" to the point that at the end of the scene, when Gumball's entire head isCovered in Gunge, he looks extremely pissed. Achievements in Ignorance: In "The Grades", when he tries to study, he has no idea where to start. When he tries to cheat, going over the material to write crib sheets lets him remember everything he needed to.
